'''Michael Wesley Redd''' (born August 24, 1979) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing {{Convert|6|ft|6|in}} tall and weighing {{Convert|215|lbs}}, he played 12 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), primarily with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Born in [[Columbus, Ohio]], Redd attended [[West High School (Columbus, Ohio)|West High School]] and later [[Ohio State University]]. As an Ohio State student, he was selected 43rd overall in the [[2000 NBA draft]]. Redd spent both his collegiate and professional career at the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. He was also a member of the [[U.S. national basketball team]] and was an [[2004 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star in 2004]].

==Early life and education==
Redd was born on August 24, 1979, in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. In his college years, Redd spent three years leading the offensive attack of The [[Ohio State University]] garnering point averages of 21.9, 19.5, and 17.5, respectively. As a sophomore, Redd and [[Scoonie Penn]] led Ohio State to the NCAA Final Four.<ref>Due to rules violations under Ohio State head coach [[Jim O'Brien (basketball, born 1949)|Jim O'Brien]], Ohio State's appearance in this tournament was stricken from NCAA records.</ref> He was then drafted after his junior year in the [[2000 NBA draft]] as a second round pick (43rd overall) by the Milwaukee Bucks.

==Professional career==

===Milwaukee Bucks (2000–2011)===
In his rookie year, Redd was not able to contribute immediately as he was behind [[National Basketball Association All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] guard [[Ray Allen]] on the depth chart. Later on, however, it became apparent that he was better than anticipated as proven by accounts that he had played extremely well against Ray Allen, [[Glenn Robinson]], and other teammates in practice. It was then that former Bucks' head coach [[George Karl]] rewarded him with additional playing time. He posted averages of 11.4 points per contest as well as 44.4% on three-point shooting during his second NBA season.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.theintelligencer.com/news/article/Redd-Expected-to-Suit-Up-for-Bucks-10561970.php|title=Redd Expected to Suit Up for Bucks|date=October 16, 2002|work=The Edwardsville Intelligencer|access-date=April 9, 2017|agency=The Associated Press}}</ref> On February 20, 2002, against the [[Houston Rockets]], Redd made eight three-point field goals in the fourth quarter, a then-NBA record. In October 2002, he signed a four-year, $12 million offer sheet with the [[Dallas Mavericks]],<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://assets.espn.go.com/nba/news/2002/1001/1439562.html|title=NBA - Mavericks sign Bucks' Redd to $12M offer sheet|last=Stein|first=Marc|date=October 14, 2002|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2017}}</ref> but it was matched by the Bucks and he remained in Milwaukee.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://assets.espn.go.com/nba/news/2002/1014/1446025.html|title=Bucks keep Redd away from Mavericks|date=October 14, 2002|access-date=April 9, 2017|agency=Associated Press|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/trainingcamp07/news/story?id=3046755|title=Disgruntled Bell back as Bucks open training camp|date=October 2, 2007|access-date=April 9, 2017|agency=Associated Press|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> During the 2003–04 season, Redd's performance, amongst other reasons (ouster of Ray Allen to Seattle via a trade), was rewarded with full starter's duties and later earning averages of 21.7 points per contest en route to his first and only [[National Basketball Association All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] appearance.

After the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], Redd signed a new contract with the Bucks that lasted six years and was worth $91 million. He chose to stay with the Bucks over leaving for his home state team, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and a chance to play for less money with [[LeBron James]].

In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Redd arguably had the best season of his career, averaging a career-high 26.7 points per game. That season, on November 11, 2006, Redd scored a career-high 57 points in a 113–111 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], breaking the single-game Bucks record for points scored set by [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] in 1971.<ref>{{cite web |title=Redd's record 57 points can't carry Bucks over Jazz |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261111015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409201233/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261111015 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 9, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 2, 2022 |date=November 11, 2006}}</ref> Later that season, on March 4, 2007, Redd scored 52 points in an overtime loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bulls get career high from Gordon to beat Bucks in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270304015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220226155017/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270304015 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 26, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 2, 2022 |date=March 4, 2007}}</ref> Despite his efforts, the Bucks struggled to win games, finishing 28–54 in the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=2006-07 Milwaukee Bucks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/2007.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=March 2, 2022}}</ref>

The Milwaukee Bucks were dealt a devastating blow January 25, 2009, when they learned Redd would miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL and MCL in his left knee. Redd missed the rest of the 2008–09 season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3859546|title=Bucks' Redd done for year with torn ACL/MCL|date=January 26, 2009|access-date=April 9, 2017|agency=Associated Press|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Redd returned for the Bucks to start the 2009–10 season, but during a game against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on January 10, 2010, he re-tore his ACL and MCL in the same knee that he had injured almost a year earlier. It was announced the next day that he would once again be lost for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com:80/2010/news/01/11/bucks.redd.ap/index.html |title=Bucks' Redd out for season with injured left knee |date=January 12, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611141546/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/01/11/bucks.redd.ap/index.html |archive-date=June 11, 2015 |url-status=dead |agency=Associated Press |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Redd tears ACL, MCL in left knee |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4817131 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 9, 2019 |date=January 11, 2010}}</ref>

On March 28, 2011, Redd was able to return to the Bucks after 14 months from the injury and recorded four assists in his return. On March 30, 2011, against the [[Toronto Raptors]], Redd scored his first NBA basket since his return from injury. Redd played 10 games in the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]]. When he left Milwaukee, he had averaged 20 points per game in his 11 seasons with the team.

===Phoenix Suns (2011–2012)===
The [[Phoenix Suns]] signed Redd to a one-year contract on December 29, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|last=Coro|first=Paul|title=Phoenix Suns sign guard Michael Redd|url=https://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2011/12/29/20111229phoenix-suns-sign-michael-redd.html|access-date=December 29, 2011|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=December 29, 2011}}</ref> Redd made his debut for Phoenix on January 12, 2012, scoring 14 points in a loss to the Cavaliers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120112/CLEPHX/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore|title=Cavaliers at Suns|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209193353/http://www.nba.com/games/20120112/CLEPHX/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore|archive-date=February 9, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Redd returned to Milwaukee on February 7, 2012, scoring 14 points in the win over the Bucks. He received a standing ovation from the crowd.<ref>{{cite web |title=Happy homecoming: Redd helps Suns down Bucks |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/15301/happy-homecoming-redd-helps-suns-down-bucks/?nid=64 |website=Arizona Sports |access-date=April 9, 2019 |date=February 8, 2012}}</ref> On March 18, 2012, Redd scored a season-high 25 points in a victory against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/recap_120318.html|title=Postgame Central: Suns Vs. Rockets|date=March 18, 2012|website=NBA.com|language=en|access-date=April 9, 2017}}</ref> In his final NBA game on April 25, 2012, he scored 14 points in a 110–106 loss to the San Antonio Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/reddmi01/gamelog/2012|title=Michael Redd 2011-12 Game Log|website=basketball-reference.com|access-date=July 7, 2022}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On November 6, 2013, Redd announced his retirement from the NBA.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9931439/michael-redd-former-member-milwaukee-bucks-retire|title=Ex-Bucks star Redd to retire in Milwaukee|date=November 5, 2013|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2017|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In his retirement Redd has become an accomplished entrepreneur and venture capitalist. He also has a popular podcast called Betting On Yourself.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michael Redd|url=https://michaelredd.com/|access-date=2020-07-24|website=Michael Redd|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, Redd was one of only three former Bucks players ([[Brandon Jennings]] and [[Marques Johnson]]) to appear in Milwaukee's [[2021 NBA Finals|championship]] parade.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hill |first1=Glynn A. |title=Milwaukee celebrates NBA championship and 'Bucks in Six Day' with a parade |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/07/22/milwaukee-bucks-parade-nba-championship/ |newspaper=Washington Post |access-date=March 2, 2022 |date=July 22, 2021}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Michael Redd Beijing Olympics Men's Semifinal Basketball.jpg|thumb|right|Redd with the [[United States national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Olympics]]]]
Redd frequently played for [[United States national basketball team|Team USA]] at the junior level and played in the [[FIBA Americas Championship|2007 FIBA Americas tournament]], a qualifying tournament for the [[2008 Summer Olympics]]. He averaged over 15 points throughout the competition. During the team's game against Puerto Rico, Redd set the qualifying record for most 3-pointers made in one game. He also set the record of most three-pointers made in the whole tournament (28) surpassing [[Penny Hardaway]] who had the previous record of 22. Redd participated in the 2008 Olympics as the team went unbeaten on the way to winning back the gold medal after defeating [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] winners [[Spain national basketball team|Spain]] and living up to their "[[2008 United States men's Olympic basketball team|Redeem Team]]" moniker after missing out on gold in the [[2004 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thamel |first1=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |title=USA Basketball Returns to the Top |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/25/sports/olympics/25bball.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=April 9, 2019 |date=August 24, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Redeem Team quieted critics -- and it would beat the Dream Team |url=https://www.si.com/olympics/2008/08/24/redeem-dream |website=SI.com |access-date=April 9, 2019 |date=August 24, 2008}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Redd, a devout [[Christians|Christian]], bought a church building for his father's ministry as the first purchase after signing his contract worth $91 million over six years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2424445|title=Redd faces toughest challenge in leadership role|date=April 27, 2006|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2017|agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The church was newly named Philadelphia Deliverance Church of Christ built in his hometown of Columbus.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/columns/story?id=2224230&columnist=wojciechowski_gene|title=Michael Redd's twist of faith|last=Wojciechowski|first=Gene|date=November 15, 2005|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2017}}</ref>

Redd, via NCT Ventures, invested in Azoti, an Ohio startup that connects producers and buyers of food.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/gallery/10-most-unlikely-startup-investments-made-by-nba-legends/slide/6/|title=10 most unlikely startup investments made by NBA legends'|last1=Mannes|first1=John|last2=Friedman|first2=Rebecca|date=July 30, 2016|website=TechCrunch|access-date=April 8, 2017}}</ref>

Redd lives in [[New Albany, Ohio]].<ref>[https://virtualglobetrotting.com/map/michael-redds-house-1/view/google/ Michael Redd's House in Powell, OH (Google Maps) (#2)] Retrieved May 21, 2018.</ref>

Redd has a son born on June 10, 2007 named Michael Redd II who pursued a career in the aviation industry rather than basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C8AVgF9vm0O/|title=Michael Redd wishes his son happy birthday}}</ref>

==In pop culture==

Rapper [[Nelly]] name-dropped Redd along with fellow NBA players [[Magic Johnson]], Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, [[Shaquille O'Neal]], and [[Allen Iverson]]—as well as NFL players [[Julius Peppers]], [[Ray Lewis]], and [[Peyton Manning]]—in the song "Heart of a Champion," the first track on 2004 album ''Sweat''. Early in the song's second verse, Nelly says: ''"... I get Buck like Michael Redd--tell 'em again: I gets Buck like Michael Redd. Heard what I said?"''<ref>{{cite web |title=Heart of a Champion |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0bFnI8KbVdM |website=YouTube.com | date=July 24, 2018 |access-date=20 May 2022}}</ref>

==Accomplishments==
* '''All-NBA Third Team''': 2004
* '''NBA All-Star''': 2004
* Held NBA record for '''most three-point field goals made in one quarter''' with '''8''' in the fourth quarter (February 20, 2002 vs. [[Houston Rockets]]); since broken by [[Klay Thompson]] on January 23, 2015.
* 5th on Milwaukee Bucks all-time points list, 5th in Milwaukee Bucks all-time scoring avg.
* Won the 1998, 1999, and 2000 Ohio State Most Valuable Player awards.
* Was 1999–00 All-Big Ten First Team in college.
* Scored a playoff career-high of 40 points against the [[Detroit Pistons]] on April 29, 2006.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121107054012/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=260429015 Redd scores 40, Ford adds 15 assists in Bucks win]</ref>
* Named to the [[United States men's national basketball team|USA Olympic basketball team]].
* '''Gold medal with Team USA, [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]]'''
* '''Gold medal with Team USA, [[2008 Summer Olympic Games]]''' (team-inducted into the Naismith Hall of Fame, class of 2025)
* Scored a career-high and Milwaukee Bucks then-franchise record 57 points against the [[Utah Jazz]] on November 11, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261111015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107054017/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261111015|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 7, 2012|title=Jazz vs. Bucks - Game Recap - November 11, 2006|date=November 11, 2006|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2017}}</ref> The record was later broken by [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]], who scored 64 points against the [[Indiana Pacers]] on December 13, 2023.
